question_text: Rotate the figure 90° CLOCKWISE.
explanation: Rotating 90° clockwise turns the top of the figure to the right side (the figure turns like a clock hand moving from 12 to 3).

question_text: Rotate the figure 90° ANTICLOCKWISE.
explanation: Rotating 90° anticlockwise turns the top of the figure to the left side (12 to 9 on a clock).

question_text: Rotate the figure 180°.
explanation: A 180° rotation turns the figure upside down: top goes to bottom AND left goes to right (it is NOT the same as a flip).

question_text: Rotate the whole figure 90° CLOCKWISE.
explanation: Rotate the figure as one block: each symbol moves 90° clockwise around the centre (top-left goes to top-right, top-right to bottom-right, etc.) and each symbol itself turns 90° clockwise.

question_text: Rotate the whole figure 90° ANTICLOCKWISE.
explanation: Rotate as one block: positions move 90° anticlockwise around the centre (top-left goes to bottom-left, etc.) and each symbol also turns 90° anticlockwise.

question_text: Rotate the figure 90° clockwise, then rotate the result 180°.
explanation: 90° clockwise followed by 180° equals 270° clockwise, which is the same as 90° anticlockwise.

question_text: Rotate the figure 90° anticlockwise, then reflect the result left-to-right (mirror image).
explanation: Do the steps in order. Step 1: rotate 90° anticlockwise. Step 2: take the mirror image (left-right reversal) of that result. Together the two steps equal a single diagonal flip of the original figure.

question_text: Rotate the figure 180°, then rotate the result 90° clockwise.
explanation: 180° + 90° clockwise = 270° clockwise (= 90° anticlockwise). Rotation sums only add when all turns are in the same direction.

question_text: Rotate the figure 90° clockwise, then flip the result top-to-bottom (water image).
explanation: Do the steps in order. Step 1: rotate 90° clockwise. Step 2: flip the result top to bottom. The two steps together equal a diagonal flip of the original.

question_text: Rotate the figure 90° clockwise, then mirror it left-to-right, then rotate it 180°.
explanation: Apply the three steps in order: 90° clockwise, then left-right mirror, then 180° rotation. Equivalent to a single diagonal flip of the original.

question_text: A square sheet is folded as shown (red dashed line = next fold) and punched. Which pattern appears when it is fully unfolded?
